neighbours.label: the word right before a particle 'off' (better off, worse off, well off, drop the kids off), i.e. predicting 'off'; also ' poor' in 'poor relation'
fire: Most retirees in the town are now much better off than their parents were.
After the storm, farmers along the coast were far worse off than inland.
Each morning her dad drops the twins off at daycare before work.
Some people believe they would be better off living in the countryside.
Families who rent are often worse off when interest rates climb.
Their grandparents were fairly well off and owned a large farm.
The bus driver let the children off right in front of the library.
In that old novel the cousin plays the poor relation who lives upstairs.
quiet: Most retirees in the town now have more savings than their parents had.
After the storm, the roads along the coast got worse than inland.
Each morning her dad takes the twins to daycare before work.
Some people believe a better life is possible in the countryside.
Families who rent often struggle when interest rates climb.
Their grandparents had a better house than anyone else on the farm.
The bus driver waited for the children in front of the library.
In that old novel the cousin is a quiet relative who lives upstairs.
